summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy with ileosigmoid anastomosis, long-term steroid use, and chronic back pain was admitted for a flare characterized by increased diarrhea (up to 20 loose stools), left lower quadrant abdominal pain, and left flank pain. The flare was likely triggered by self-reduction of prednisone to 5 mg daily. Workup showed no infectious cause, with negative stool cultures and C. difficile testing. Renal ultrasound was normal, and lumbar MRI showed no new spinal pathology. The patient improved with IV and then oral prednisone, with bowel movements returning to baseline. Pain was managed with IV Dilaudid, transitioned to oral oxycodone. He was discharged on prednisone 40 mg daily, calcium, vitamin D, and a 10-day supply of oxycodone, with follow-up arranged with GI and spine specialists. A hospital bed was provided for home use to aid positioning and comfort.
